findings.title: Conditional passkeys UI no longer rendered on fresh (no-user) login
findings.body: In authenticate(), the new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires the user to be non-null before calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. Previously the form was filled exactly in the opposite case — inside the `else` branch where `context.getUser() == null` (fresh login, no user selected yet). On a normal first login there is no user in the context, so the WebAuthn conditional UI attributes (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI) are never set, the browser never triggers `navigator.credentials.get()` with conditional mediation, and passkey autofill / discoverable-key login on the initial login page silently stops working. The same regression exists in `challenge(context, error, field)` at line 137: for the user-not-found error path (user == null) the webauthn context (including the AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE auth note that the webauthn action later reads) is no longer populated, so a subsequent passkey attempt from that error page would fail with a null challenge. The user-null check should not be part of deciding whether to render conditional passkeys; it should only distinguish the re-authentication case.

findings.title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match any declared method
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method added in this PR is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm (line 160). No no-arg overload is declared in UsernamePasswordForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or any other file changed in this PR. Unless an overload exists elsewhere, this is a compilation error; if one does exist elsewhere with different semantics, the call site needs to be verified against the new re-authentication behavior introduced here.

findings.title: Absence assertions for webauthn form catch generic Exception
findings.body: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey verifies the webauthn form is absent with try { findElement(...); fail(); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }. Catching generic Exception means any failure — including assertion errors from the MatcherAssert line itself or unrelated WebDriver errors — is silently treated as 'expected', so the test can pass even when the page is broken. Catch NoSuchElementException specifically (as done elsewhere in this same file via Assert.assertThrows).
